evals.prompt: Write a Pi extension that blocks any bash command containing `curl` unless the user confirms, and logs all blocked commands to a file at ~/.pi/agent/blocked-commands.log
evals.expected_output: A TypeScript extension file that hooks into tool_call events, checks for curl in bash commands, prompts via ctx.ui.select, and appends blocked commands to a log file. Should check ctx.hasUI and handle non-interactive mode.
assertions: Uses correct ExtensionAPI import from @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
Hooks into tool_call event (the correct event for intercepting tool calls)
Checks event.toolName === 'bash' before inspecting command
Tests for curl in the command string
Checks ctx.hasUI before calling interactive UI methods
Uses ctx.ui.select or ctx.ui.confirm for user confirmation
Returns { block: true, reason: '...' } to prevent execution
Logs blocked commands to ~/.pi/agent/blocked-commands.log
Uses correct export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI) signature

evals.prompt: I want to set up Pi to use Ollama with llama3.2 locally, with auto-compaction disabled and a custom session directory at ~/pi-sessions. Walk me through the configuration.
evals.expected_output: Instructions covering models.json with Ollama provider config (baseUrl localhost:11434/v1, api openai-completions, dummy apiKey, model id llama3.2), settings.json with compaction.enabled=false and sessionDir pointing to ~/pi-sessions.
assertions: Provides models.json with Ollama baseUrl containing localhost:11434
Uses api type openai-completions (correct for Ollama)
Includes model entry with id llama3.2
Provides settings.json with compaction.enabled set to false
Sets sessionDir to ~/pi-sessions
Correct file paths: ~/.pi/agent/models.json and ~/.pi/agent/settings.json

evals.prompt: Create a Pi skill that helps with database migrations — it should know about Prisma, Drizzle, and raw SQL approaches. Give me the full SKILL.md and any reference files.
evals.expected_output: A SKILL.md with proper frontmatter (name, description), a main body routing to reference files, and separate reference docs for Prisma, Drizzle, and raw SQL migration patterns.
assertions: SKILL.md has valid YAML frontmatter with name and description fields
Name follows Pi convention: lowercase, hyphens only, max 64 chars
Description mentions trigger contexts (migrations, Prisma, Drizzle, SQL)
Includes separate reference files for Prisma, Drizzle, and raw SQL
SKILL.md uses relative paths to reference files
Body routes to the correct reference doc based on the user's framework choice

evals.prompt: Add the GitHub MCP server (https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/, token in GITHUB_TOKEN) to Pi for all my projects. It has ~90 tools, so keep them out of the model's tool list, but make search_code directly callable. Check that it works.
evals.expected_output: An entry in ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json under mcpServers with the url, an Authorization header referencing ${GITHUB_TOKEN}, a non-direct server exposure (codemode, codemode-deferred, or deferred), and toolExposure making search_code direct; then pi mcp list to verify and /reload for a running session.
assertions: Writes the server to ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json (global), not settings.json and not the project .pi/mcp.json
Uses the mcpServers object with a url field (streamable HTTP), not an sse type
Keeps the secret out of the file with "Authorization": "Bearer ${GITHUB_TOKEN}" (or pi mcp add --bearer-token-env-var GITHUB_TOKEN)
Sets server exposure to codemode, codemode-deferred, or deferred rather than direct
Uses toolExposure with "search_code": "direct"
Runs pi mcp list to verify the connection
Tells the user to /reload or start a new session so a running session connects
Does not tell the user to install an MCP extension or package, since MCP is built in

evals.prompt: My Pi permission extension asks before every bash call. It works for direct calls, but when the model runs bash from a codemode script the approval lookup fails because my code searches the last assistant message for event.toolCallId. Fix the extension so codemode calls are gated too.
evals.expected_output: A tool_call handler that judges each call from the event itself, recognises nested calls by event.parentToolCallId (ids like <parent>/<n>), does not require the id to exist in the assistant message, does not auto-approve children because the codemode call was approved, and blocks when there is no UI.
assertions: Keeps using the tool_call event and checks event.toolName === 'bash' (or isToolCallEventType('bash', event))
Explains that nested calls carry event.parentToolCallId and have ids of the form <parent id>/<n> that never appear in the transcript
Stops requiring the tool call id to be found in the last assistant message for nested calls
Reads the command from event.input for the nested call instead of parsing the codemode script
Does not approve a nested call just because the parent codemode call was approved
Does not rely on the nestedCalls record on the tool result for approval
Checks ctx.hasUI and returns { block: true, reason } when no UI is available
Notes that a blocked nested call makes the script's tools.bash() promise reject

evals.prompt: I have a Pi extension tool `list_issues` that returns a text table. When the model calls it from codemode, the script gets a string it has to parse. Change the tool so codemode scripts get the issue objects, and keep the model's view readable.
evals.expected_output: The tool declares outputSchema (TypeBox) and returns structuredContent matching it on every result, alongside the existing text content; failures that still carry data use isError: true; read-only annotations are set.
assertions: Adds an outputSchema built with typebox Type.Object/Type.Array
Returns structuredContent matching the schema on every result
Keeps model-facing text in content
Explains that codemode scripts receive structuredContent instead of the text only when outputSchema is declared
Uses isError: true (not a thrown error) for a failure that should still return data, or throws for plain failures
Keeps structuredContent JSON-compatible (no Date objects, Maps, or class instances)
Marks the tool with annotations such as readOnlyHint: true if it does not modify anything
Does not claim the model itself receives structuredContent

evals.prompt: Write a Pi extension that uses the Jev classifier to decide whether a user prompt is a question or a coding task, and sets a status line accordingly. It should not break when TypeSafe is down or the key is missing.
evals.expected_output: An extension that finds the classifier with ctx.modelRegistry.findOfType('classifier', 'typesafe', 'jev-latest'), calls ctx.modelRegistry.classify with a choice or bool question and ctx.signal, checks stopReason and the answer type before using probabilities, and falls back cleanly when the model is missing or the result is an error.
assertions: Uses ctx.modelRegistry.findOfType('classifier', 'typesafe', 'jev-latest') or getModelOfType with type 'classifier'
Handles the classifier model being undefined
Calls ctx.modelRegistry.classify(model, { state, questions }, { signal })
Uses a valid question shape: type 'choice' with a criteria record, or type 'bool' with criteria { true, false }
Checks result.stopReason === 'stop' before reading answers, and handles 'error' and 'aborted'
Does not wrap classify() in try/catch as the only error handling, since it returns error results instead of rejecting
Checks the answer type (choice/bool) before reading probabilities or probability
Mentions TYPESAFE_API_KEY (or another Jev provider credential) as the auth requirement

evals.prompt: I'm embedding Pi with the SDK. My host sends user input with session.prompt() while idle and session.steer() while streaming, then waits for agent_settled before showing 'done'. Sometimes it hangs forever on inputs that one of my extensions handles as a command. I also drive a separate Pi over RPC. How do I fix both?
evals.expected_output: Explains dispositions: session.steer()/followUp() return 'queued' or 'handled'; session.prompt() returns nothing and resolves after an accepted run finishes, so the SDK host should await it instead of waiting for agent_settled; RPC prompt responses carry data.disposition 'started' | 'queued' | 'handled' (steer/follow_up 'queued' | 'handled'); on 'handled' no run started, so the client must not wait for agent_settled. Shows code that branches on the disposition.
assertions: States that session.steer() and session.followUp() return 'queued' or 'handled'
States that an RPC prompt response has data.disposition of 'started', 'queued', or 'handled'
Explains that 'handled' means no run started for that input, so the client must not wait for agent_settled
Uses agent_settled (not agent_end) as the completion signal when a run did start
Shows RpcClient.prompt()/steer()/followUp() returning the disposition, or reads data.disposition from the raw response
Notes that session.prompt() resolves after an accepted run finishes
Does not suggest a timeout as the fix
